record.original_question: For each Euclidean dimension d, classify all k-orbit realizations in E^d of regular d-polytopes under the restriction k ≤ d.

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Find all k-orbit realizations in E^d of regular d-polytopes for k ≤ d.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be an abstract regular $d$-polytope, i.e., a ranked poset of rank $d$ whose automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts transitively on its flags (maximal chains). A realization of $\mathcal{P}$ in Euclidean space $\mathbb{E}^d$ is a mapping $\beta$ from the vertex set of $\mathcal{P}$ into $\mathbb{E}^d$ together with a homomorphism from $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ into the Euclidean isometry group of $\mathbb{E}^d$ such that $\beta$ is equivariant. The realization induces, in the natural way, maps on all faces of $\mathcal{P}$, and hence a geometric polytope $P\subset \mathbb{E}^d$ together with a symmetry subgroup $G(P)\le \mathrm{Isom}(\mathbb{E}^d)$. The number of flag orbits of $P$ under $G(P)$ is called the orbit number; $P$ is said to be a $k$-orbit realization of $\mathcal{P}$ if $G(P)$ has exactly $k$ orbits on the flags of $P$.

Problem: For each integer $d\ge 1$ and each integer $k$ with $1\le k\le d$, classify all $k$-orbit realizations in $\mathbb{E}^d$ of abstract regular $d$-polytopes.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of classifying realizations of abstract regular polytopes in Euclidean space, refined by the number of flag orbits, is a well-known ongoing program. Surveys and recent works (e.g., Schulte's chapter in the Handbook of Discrete and Computational Geometry, McMullen's "Geometric Regular Polytopes", and Matteo's thesis on polytopes with few flag orbits) treat partial cases but do not provide a complete classification for all $d$ and $k\le d$. No source found announcing a full solution.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry of Polytopes and Polyhedra (Handbook chapter, Schulte)
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of realizations of abstract regular polytopes in Euclidean spaces remains an outstanding problem.
status_evidence.claim: The classification problem for realizations of abstract regular polytopes is open in general.

status_evidence.title: Convex Polytopes and Tilings with Few Flag Orbits (Matteo)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies convex polytopes with few flag orbits, providing partial classifications.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial classifications for small numbers of flag orbits are known.

status_evidence.title: Realizations of Polytopes — Geometric Regular Polytopes (McMullen)
status_evidence.snippet: General theory of realizations of regular polytopes in Euclidean space.
status_evidence.claim: The general theory exists but a full classification by flag-orbit number is not given.
